app.title: NoiseQ+ v4.0 — Road Traffic Noise Health Impact Assessment Tool
app.summary: A person moves through a guided multi-page form. First they name the area, enter the population size and give the exposure distribution. They can type the percentage of people in each fixed band, which must add up to 100%, or give one threshold with the share above it and let the tool estimate the bands. Next they choose which health outcomes to include, set the reference level and replace the default baseline rates if they have local ones. The tool then works out the attributable cases or deaths, intervals, rates, attributable fractions and DALYs for each outcome. Finally the person checks how much the results move under other reference levels, other risk estimates and other weight sets, and exports the results as CSV or prints them.

task.text: Estimate the yearly cases, deaths and DALYs attributable to an environmental exposure in a population, and check how much the estimate depends on its assumptions.

data.text: A population size and the share of that population in each band of a fixed set of exposure bands, plus a fixed set of health outcomes. Each outcome has a relative risk with its interval or an exposure-response function, a baseline rate the person can edit, and disability weights.
data.item: a health outcome estimated for the assessed population, from the share of people in each exposure band

stage.text: estimating the attributable burden from exposure-map summaries, and testing it under other assumptions before reporting

mechanism.text: A tabbed stepper opens each page only once the page before it has been reached. Two input forms (exposure and outcomes) feed calculations that are recomputed whenever an input changes. Their results appear on a results page with tables and a bar chart, and on a sensitivity page with scenario tables that mark the row in use. A methods page draws the dose-response curves and the evidence behind the parameters.

field.text: comparative risk assessment of noise exposure in environmental epidemiology

workflow.name: estimate the burden attributable to an exposure across a population, then test it under other assumptions

steps.here: Type the location, country and population size. Then either enter the percentage of the population in each of seven 5 dB Lden bands (a running total must reach 100% before Continue works), or pick a threshold and the % above it and let the tool spread it across the bands.

steps.step: choose which outcomes and parameters to apply
steps.here: Tick health outcomes on cards that show each one's relative risk and source, optionally override the 53 dB reference level, edit baseline rates per 100,000 (edited ones are tagged Custom), and pick the Lden-to-Lnight offset.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For each outcome, compute the attributable fraction from relative risk per band, or the number affected from a polynomial exposure-response function. Show cases or deaths with 95% CI, the rate, the PAF and DALYs split into YLD and YLL, with a bar chart and a total row.

steps.step: compare the result under alternative assumptions
steps.here: Scenario tables recompute IHD cases under four relative-risk sources, cases and DALYs at reference levels of 45, 50, 53 and 55 dB, and annoyance and sleep DALYs under three disability-weight sets, with the row in use highlighted.
Export CSV writes the location, parameters, a row for each outcome with intervals, and the YLD, YLL and DALY totals. Print / PDF uses a print layout that hides the navigation.

steps.step: check the method behind the numbers
steps.here: A methods page shows the formulas, line charts of the dose-response and relative-risk curves, an evidence table for each outcome, the DALY parameters and the limitations.

distinctive: Two calculation routes sit side by side: an attributable fraction from relative risk per 10 dB above a counterfactual, scaled by a baseline rate, and a polynomial exposure-response function that gives the share of people affected directly.
Every estimate has a central value and a range from the confidence interval of the relative risk or from the spread of disability weights.
The burden is split into years lived with disability for morbidity outcomes and years of life lost for the mortality outcome, then summed into DALYs.
When only a share above a threshold is known, the tool estimates the full band distribution by decay weighting.
Nighttime exposure is derived from the day-evening-night metric with an offset the person chooses.

parts.title: Guided step tabs
parts.summary: Numbered tabs for the six pages, where only pages already reached can be clicked, so the person goes through the assessment in order.

spans.first: const PAGES=["Welcome","Location and Population","Health Data","Results","Sensitivity Analysis","Methods"];

parts.title: Location, population and exposure distribution
parts.summary: A form for the area, the population size and the share of people in each noise band, entered as detailed bands or as a single threshold. A running total must reach 100%, and the Lnight offset is chosen here.

parts.title: Health outcomes, reference level and baseline rates
parts.summary: Checkbox cards choose which outcomes to estimate. The reference level can be overridden, and each incidence outcome's baseline rate per 100,000 can be edited and is tagged when it is custom.

parts.title: Attributable cases and DALYs
parts.summary: Shows attributable cases or deaths with 95% CI, the rate and the PAF for each outcome, the number of people affected for each exposure-response outcome, a bar chart of cases, and a DALY table that adds YLD and YLL into a total.

parts.title: Export CSV and print
parts.summary: Downloads a CSV of the parameters, each outcome's estimates with intervals and the burden totals, or prints the page for a PDF report.

parts.title: Sensitivity analysis
parts.summary: Recomputes the burden under alternative relative-risk sources, reference levels and disability-weight sets, and shows each as a scenario table with the row in use highlighted.

parts.title: Methods, dose-response curves and references
parts.summary: Explains the calculation steps and formulas, draws the exposure-response and relative-risk curves as line charts, and lists the evidence for each outcome, the DALY parameters, the limitations and the references.
